home.eyebrow: Hyperopic reserve program for children and adults, ages 5–45 · Ortho-K: precise corneal reshaping
home.title: Clear vision all day, no glasses. 30 years, one focus.
home.mark: Building your child’s hyperopic reserve so their prescription stops increasing.
home.lead: Your child sleeps in highly oxygen-permeable, semi-soft lenses. In the morning, they take them out and see clearly. Ortho-K slows nearsightedness as children grow, and for children with a family history of nearsightedness it is the best option for effective control.
home.introTitle: Is your child’s prescription going up every year?
home.introLead: Nearsightedness often gets worse during the school years. Stronger glasses fix the blur, but they don’t slow the change.
home.visitTitle: What happens at the first visit
home.visit1: We talk with you about your child’s eyes and daily routine.
home.visit2: Your child has a full eye exam and a map of the front of the eye.
home.visit3: Dr. Woo explains the results and answers your questions.

faq.title: Parent questions
faq.q2: What age can my child start?
faq.q3: Is it hard for kids to put in the lenses?
faq.placeholder: Placeholder answer. Dr. Woo’s team will write this in plain words for parents.
faq.a1: Ortho-K is a safe choice for children when an eye doctor fits the lenses and your family cares for them exactly as instructed. Like any contact lens worn overnight, it carries a small risk of eye infection, which can be serious. You can keep that risk low by washing your hands before touching the lenses; cleaning and storing them only with the solutions we give you, never with tap water; replacing the case and lenses on schedule; and coming to every follow-up visit so Dr. Woo can check your child’s eyes. If your child has eye pain, redness, sensitivity to light, discharge, or blurry vision that doesn’t clear, take the lenses out and call us right away at (800) 991-8881.

about.title: Dr. Paul T. Woo, Optometrist
about.lead: Dr. Woo is the founder and clinical director of 1234 Ortho-K Vision Care.
about.bio1: Dr. Woo graduated with a bachelor’s degree from the University of California, Irvine, and went on to earn his Doctor of Optometry degree from the Southern California College of Optometry.
about.bio2: As orthokeratology evolved from day wear to night wear, so did Dr. Woo. Today, he treats children who want to keep their myopia from progressing and who are able to see well all day just by wearing lenses while they sleep.
about.bio3: Dr. Woo is a former president of the San Gabriel Valley Optometric Association.
about.bio4: He wants to continue working with other doctors to expand the acceptance and success of orthokeratology, so that more nearsighted patients can protect their vision.
about.staff: Our friendly, dedicated, and highly trained staff is always happy to serve and help our patients through every step of the process.

steps.title: Your treatment, step by step
steps.s1: You fill in a full medical history form, and we measure your child’s eyes with computerized refraction.
steps.s2: A slit-lamp exam and a dilated eye exam. Dr. Woo talks with you about your needs and sets the direction of treatment.
steps.s3: You go over the report with our consultant and settle the treatment plan and fees.
steps.s4: Dilating drops or lenses custom-designed for your child, and lessons in eye and lens hygiene.
steps.s5: The correction phase lasts three to six months, with routine checks to adjust the lenses.
steps.s6: We book regular follow-up visits to keep track of your child’s eyes.
